resources.string: Continue in the current view. The next command appears when it is available.
Guide me one step at a time
This choice could not be saved for next time.

Build an image from layers. For example, add a text layer, enter a title and choose Apply. Changes are kept as a local draft; Save commits a project version. Export makes a separate image. Choose location on the result to copy it outside Halo.

Write in the note or use Add for a heading, checklist or image. For example, make a shopping list and check off an item. Watch the saved or draft status before leaving. Apply Markdown source changes explicitly. Export creates a separate text file; it does not replace the note.

Arrange text and source cards on a board. Use Add, then choose the kind of card. For example, place a note beside a photo. A linked card refers to its original; a copy is a separate object. Select a card to inspect it. Fit all cards brings the whole board into view.

Review information Halo may use later. Open a memory to correct it or deliberately forget it. For example, correct an outdated preference. Forgetting a memory does not delete its source file. Suggestions need your review before they become remembered context.

Start with a goal and optional source material. For example, choose a note and ask to practise its main ideas. Review the source and model availability before starting. A saved lesson can be reopened. Type an answer, ask for help or use practice cards; Back returns without submitting an answer.

Library holds your saved work. Search, filter or sort to find an item, then open it. Returning keeps your current view and reveals the item if it still matches. Tools opens the five instrument families. Import keeps a local copy of a file you choose.

You can type instead of talking. Choose Help for ideas about what to say. Stop ends the current voice action. A grown-up handles protected settings. Asking for help does not send your work or turn on the microphone.
Choose a learning goal, then continue to material.
Choose source material, or enter a topic before continuing.
Choose the learning style and continue to review the options.
Review the source and choose an available model, then start the lesson.
